rationale: The flagged contradiction holds up. The moderate ipTM of about 0.6 therefore can't offset the lack of co-expression, and both ectodomains are N-glycosylated, which AF3 does not model. I'm lowering the verdict from CONFIRMED_NOVEL to IMPLAUSIBLE with low confidence. Brain RNA-level overlap or a cell-type-specific contact could still exist, but the data I have don't show one.

GPR34 is a lysophosphatidylserine (lipid) GPCR with no known protein ligand, and the large interface (BSA 2816 Å2, 648 contacts) may be transmembrane-helix packing made without a bilayer; I could not check where the interface falls because no fold was run.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt: ICOSLG has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its Ig ectodomain, by my reading of the topology); GPR34 has the Glycoprotein keyword and 5 glycosylation sites (on its extracellular N-terminus/loops, likewise inferred). The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing relevant (ICOSLG 1 unrelated hit; GPR34 8 hits on pharmacology and lymphoma). Any extracellular interface would likely involve glycosylated regions on both sides, but whether a site sits on the modeled interface was not verified.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence count is 0.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: no interaction match (GPR34 is not in its gene table). PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. The pair is novel as far as these sources go.
follow_up: Inspect the AF3 model to see whether the interface is transmembrane-helix packing or ectodomain contact, and whether it mixes cytoplasmic and extracellular residues. Map the UniProt N-glycosylation sites of both proteins onto the interface, and if any land on it, re-fold with glycans attached. Canonical ICOSLG–ICOS binding and LysoPS–GPR34 binding are the expected real interactions; a wet-lab test (co-immunoprecipitation or a cell-surface binding assay in macrophages) is needed before pursuing this pair.

rationale: HPA classes MST1 (macrophage stimulating 1) as secreted to blood and GPR37 as a membrane GPCR, so a ligand-receptor pairing is topologically plausible, and STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned no hit for the pair. Confidence is low because the AF3 ipTM of 0.52 is only just above the 0.5 threshold, the supplied p_twoway is 0.050, and the glycosylation caveat on GPR37 could not be checked against the interface. The MST1 UniProt lookup returned the wrong protein (STK4, the Hippo kinase aliased "MST1", Q13043), so no valid UniProt mechanism or PTM data was obtained for the MST1 side.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: GPR37: UniProt lists the Glycoprotein keyword and 3 glycosylation sites, and the extracellular side is where a secreted ligand would bind, so a glycan at the modelled interface is possible but was not verified. MST1: uniprot_annotation returned STK4 (Q13043), not the macrophage stimulating protein, so its PTM data does not apply; the pubmed_ptm_glycosylation hits for MST1 (406) are likewise dominated by STK4/Hippo papers and are uninformative. No per-residue interface check was done, so there is not enough to call LIKELY_ARTIFACT_PTM.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits. The symbol "MST1" is ambiguous with STK4 in the literature, so even a nonzero count would have needed disambiguation.
known_interaction_evidence: STRING: not found. CellPhoneDB: not found. PubMed co-occurrence: 0 hits. No evidence anywhere of a known interaction. UniProt lists prosaposin, osteocalcin and neuroprotectin D1 as GPR37 ligands; MST1 is not among them.
follow_up: 1) Re-pull UniProt for the correct MST1 protein (macrophage stimulating protein, P26927 from background knowledge) to get its glycosylation sites and domain structure. 2) MST1R (RON) is listed under other_subunits from background knowledge as the established MST1 receptor, not from any tool result; fold MST1–MST1R as a positive-control benchmark for the 0.52 ipTM. 3) Check whether the modelled interface falls on GPR37's extracellular N-terminus or loops rather than cytoplasmic residues, and whether any of the 3 GPR37 N-glycosylation sites sit on it; if so, re-fold with the glycan attached. 4) Test binding and signalling experimentally, e.g. MST1-induced ERK phosphorylation or internalisation in GPR37-expressing cells, with prosaposin as a positive control.

rationale: The check says HPA gives no route for these two to meet. Neither protein is secreted, so contact would need them in the same place, and HPA shows zero shared protein-level tissue (PLXNB3 in brain/glia, GPRC5A in lung/bladder). Both are plasma-membrane proteins, so there is no compartment mismatch. That only makes a meeting possible in principle, and nothing observed supports it. The data also give no positive evidence: STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed all returned nothing for this pair (known_interaction_strength=none), and the AF3 model was marginal (ipTM 0.52, interface pLDDT 60.2, minimum interface PAE 10.46 Å). The flagged fold status is "not_run", so there is no separate structural result to weigh. PLXNB3's 8 glycosylation sites are unrepresented in AF3, which weakens the model further. I am moving from INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE to IMPLAUSIBLE because the absence of shared tissue combined with the weak model leaves no substantiated reason to expect these proteins to interact. Confidence stays low because HPA tissue data are coarse and low-level co-expression in some cells cannot be ruled out.

cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-mention count is 0 for PLXNB3 and GPRC5A.

follow_up: Check for any co-expression in single-cell data (e.g. glia or cancer cell lines) before discarding this entirely. If co-expression is found, re-run AF3 with the glycans modeled.

rationale: The pair is compartment-plausible (TNC secreted to the extracellular matrix, GPR75 a plasma-membrane GPCR) and has no hit in STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed, so it is novel. However, TNC is a heavily glycosylated proteoglycan (24 UniProt glycosylation sites) and GPR75 carries 3 glycosylation sites, none of which AF3 modeled. The supplied fold metrics are also weak: ipTM 0.51 is borderline, interface pLDDT is 57.7, min separation of 1.55 Å indicates clashes, and a 7229 Å2 interface with 1587 contacts is implausibly large for a GPCR's small ectodomain, so it probably spans transmembrane or cytoplasmic regions a secreted protein cannot reach.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt annotates TNC as Glycoprotein and Proteoglycan with 24 glycosylation sites and 42 disulfide bonds, and GPR75 as Glycoprotein with 3 glycosylation sites. Both sets of glycans are on the extracellular surfaces where any real contact would occur, so they are plausibly relevant to the modeled interface. The PubMed PTM searches (134 hits for TNC, 11 for GPR75) returned nothing specific to glycosylation. No per-residue check of glycan sites against the interface was done.

follow_up: No fold was run here. Re-fold a truncated construct (individual TNC domains such as the FN-III repeats or fibrinogen globe against GPR75) rather than the 2741-token full complex. Then check the interface topology (extracellular only versus transmembrane/cytoplasmic) and whether the N-glycan sites on GPR75's N-terminus and extracellular loops, or on TNC, fall on the interface. If a confident extracellular interface survives (chain-pair ipTM above 0.5, no clashes), re-fold with glycans attached before any wet-lab binding assay.

rationale: No prior record of this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, PubMed co-occurrence 0), and a secreted protein (B2M, "Secreted to blood") against a plasma-membrane orphan GPCR (GPR82, UniProt "Cell membrane") is compartment-compatible. cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for B2M with GPR82.

rationale: No prior evidence links this pair (STRING not found, CellPhoneDB not found, 0 PubMed co-mentions), and expression/compartment do not rule it out. I could not check whether any glycosylation site actually sits on the modeled interface, so the artifact call rests on general plausibility, not a per-residue finding.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: IGF2R (UniProt P11717): Glycoprotein, Lipoprotein/Palmitate; 18 glycosylation sites, 59 disulfide bonds; function is binding phosphomannosyl (M6P) residues on lysosomal enzymes, i.e. a glycan-mediated mechanism. GPR82 (Q96P67): Glycoprotein with 2 glycosylation sites. The PubMed PTM search gave 56 hits for IGF2R (the top titles are mostly not about PTMs) and 0 for GPR82. With about 2,832 Å² of buried surface on the heavily glycosylated IGF2R ectodomain, glycan interference at the modeled contact is plausible, but whether any site lies on the interface was not checked.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 papers mentioning IGF2R and GPR82 together.

follow_up: Map the modeled interface residues against IGF2R's 18 and GPR82's 2 UniProt N-glycosylation sites, and check membrane topology of the interface (that it does not combine cytoplasmic and extracellular residues). Re-fold using only the relevant IGF2R domain repeats plus GPR82, with glycans attached, to see whether ipTM rises clearly above 0.5; the current 2,827-token fold with interface pLDDT 52 and 1.79 Å minimum separation is marginal. IGF2R has 116 known interactors (HPA), so a promiscuous or non-specific contact with a large ectodomain is also possible. If the interface survives, test by co-immunoprecipitation in macrophage/Kupffer-like cells.

rationale: The check is right that HPA gives no shared protein-level tissue and that neither protein is secreted, so the data show no demonstrated route for contact. That lowers my confidence in the pair. It does not amount to the compartment mismatch that would justify IMPLAUSIBLE. Both CSPG4 and MRGPRF are plasma-membrane proteins, so they could in principle meet in cis or in trans on neighbouring cells. My earlier pull also showed single-cell RNA overlap in vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. That overlap is RNA-only and weaker than protein-level overlap. Missing protein-level overlap for an orphan GPCR such as MRGPRF is also weak evidence, because antibody coverage for GPCRs is poor. The pair is novel (no STRING, CellPhoneDB or PubMed hit), and no fold was run, so there is no structural support or structural refutation. The glycosylation concern (CSPG4 has 16 sites, MRGPRF has 1) is untested, and neither protein is a lectin. I therefore do not lean on it. Overall, the pair has no positive evidence for an interaction and no decisive evidence against one.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: CSPG4 is a chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan with 16 glycosylation sites. MRGPRF has 1. No fold was run, so neither was checked against an interface. Neither protein is a lectin. The concern is hypothetical.
cooccurrence_evidence: pubmed_cooccurrence returned 0 hits for CSPG4 + MRGPRF.

follow_up: Look for protein-level expression of MRGPRF in CSPG4-positive pericytes or smooth muscle cells. If that is supported, run an AF3 fold, including glycan-aware modelling for the CSPG4 ectodomain.

The PubMed PTM searches returned nothing specific to glycosylation of either protein at an interface. Glycans on the extracellular regions are an extra caveat for any modeled ectodomain contact, but the verdict does not rest on this.

rationale: The flagged contradiction holds. PPIA passed the confidence gate against 4 of the 11 receptors in this screen (36%), so the fold says more about PPIA than about GPR63. I see no biological reason for that breadth. PPIA is a small, abundant peptidyl-prolyl isomerase with about 195 known interactors, and its one established receptor is BSG/CD147, not a GPCR. The breadth looks like partner-driven stickiness, and the ipTM of 0.5 sits only at threshold, so CONFIRMED_NOVEL overstated the evidence. Nothing else contradicts the pair. STRING, CellPhoneDB and PubMed co-occurrence all show no prior record, and HPA compartments are plausible, with PPIA secreted and GPR63 at the plasma membrane. That is why I'm not calling it IMPLAUSIBLE, but compartment plausibility alone doesn't establish specificity. GPR63's 3 glycosylation sites were never checked against the interface, which is a further unresolved caveat. The pair is unsupported rather than confirmed.
ptm_glycosylation_evidence: UniProt lists 3 glycosylation sites on GPR63 and 1 on PPIA. Their position relative to the interface was not checked. PPIA also binds heparan sulfate. This is a caveat, not evidence of an artifact.
cooccurrence_evidence: PubMed co-occurrence for PPIA and GPR63 returned 0 papers.
